text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "eligibility/rules.py already has is_eligible(household: Household, score: int | None = None, today=None) -> bool. It returns False if household.status != \"active\" (line 21), otherwise computes score = vulnerability_score(household, today) if score is None else score (line 23), and returns score >= threshold_for(household) (line 24). A needs_review implementation can reuse this exact signature pattern and the score parameter.", "file": "eligibility/rules.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "threshold_for(household: Household) -> int is defined at eligibility/rules.py line 16; the module comment at line 6 says 'A household qualifies when its vulnerability score reaches the threshold.' Tests confirm thresholds: a household with only an adult has threshold 60, an adult plus pregnant member has threshold 45 (tests/test_eligibility.py lines 26-27).", "file": "eligibility/rules.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "vulnerability_score(household: Household, today=None) -> int is at eligibility/scoring.py lines 32-33: it returns min(100, sum(score_breakdown(household, today).values())). This is the score the ticket says to use.", "file": "eligibility/scoring.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "Household model (core/models.py line 31) has status: str = \"active\" with values active | inactive | merged. is_eligible only treats status == \"active\" as eligible, so needs_review must also check household.status != \"active\" to return False for inactive/merged households.", "file": "core/models.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "registry/register.py line 11: load_households(*, active_only: bool = False) -> list[Household]; with active_only=True it filters to households with status == \"active\" (lines 12-13). Useful for iterating active households.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "Existing test data confirms the near-miss scenario: tests/test_eligibility.py line 34 asserts vulnerability_score(h, DAY) == 58 and not is_eligible(h, today=DAY) — a household scoring 58 against a 60 threshold is not eligible but is within 5 points, i.e. exactly a near-miss case. Line 37 asserts a household with score 45 and threshold 45 IS eligible, so needs_review must not flag households whose score >= threshold.", "file": "tests/test_eligibility.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "is_eligible accepts an optional precomputed score parameter (score: int | None = None), so callers that already computed vulnerability_score can pass it to avoid recomputation; needs_review should follow the same convention for consistency.", "file": "eligibility/rules.py"}]}}
